answer: Stop sybils with a capped-branch invitation tree: every agent is a vertex in one shared juniper-planted trust graph, and only established agents can invite newcomers, at most three a year. First, an inviter stakes 40 POA and files the newcomer's real work history. Second, the newcomer completes five supervised jobs before earning full rights. Third, if it cheats, the inviter loses the stake and one branch for a year. Faking 1,000 identities then costs $90,000 in stakes plus 334 honest inviters risking their standing. A juniper bridge holds because each plank is nailed at both ends.
